MAJOR: `should_enforce` drops the former fail-closed behavior for items with missing/empty `created_at`: those items now silently fall out of enforcement (returns False) instead of being flagged. The prior review recorded this as ACTIONED, but the new code reopens a fail-open hole for any item lacking `created_at`.

`duration_ms` plumbing in `architect_review.main` uses `time.time()` with no `import time` added in the diff and no test exercising `main()`/`_ingest(duration_ms=...)`; if `time` is not already imported this is a NameError on the review ingestion path, and either way the new telemetry path is untested.

`gate1_check.evaluate`/`main` reach into private members of other modules (`ar._get_item`, `dpack._cfg`) and re-implement the config/error-handling wrapper instead of exposing a supported `design_pack.evaluate(item_id)` API; this couples two gates to internal signatures and duplicates the fail-closed exception logic already present in `design_pack.check`.
MINOR: `should_enforce` compares `created_at` to `enforce_from` by raw lexicographic string comparison; partial or non-ISO values (e.g. `2026-10-2`, timezone-suffixed timestamps, date-only vs datetime) can misclassify without any parse/validation.

`config/design-pack.json` hardcodes `enforce_items: ["BI-PF-1484","BI-PF-1485"]` with no removal policy or documented lifecycle; this allowlist will grow monotonically in shared config and silently re-assert enforcement on already-closed items.
`gate_metrics` is labeled "Gate metrics" but iterates every trail event (implementation, tests, etc.); either filter by gate stage or rename, otherwise the section overstates what is measured.

`final_rows` in `show` hardcodes the pointer "see section 10 (per-gate time/tokens/cost)"; the same diff already renumbers sections, so this cross-reference will silently go stale on the next section insert.

`finalize_item.build` persists `gate_metrics` alongside `usage`, duplicating token/cost data in the final report with no stated source-of-truth; downstream consumers may reconcile the two and diverge when `price_usage` is applied differently.
NIT: `gate_metrics` applies `price_usage` per event while `usage_totals` totals separately; a brief comment on why totals and per-gate rows must agree (or a shared aggregation) would prevent drift.

`PLACEHOLDERS` set ordering/contents differ slightly from the original inline tuples only by centralization; consider unit-testing the constant's behavior directly so future edits to the set are treated as gate-visible.
SUMMARY: Solid direction: per-gate telemetry, config-driven design-pack enforcement at Gate 1, and the final-report gate-metrics addition are coherent and mostly well-tested. Top risks are the reopened fail-closed hole for missing `created_at`, untested/unverified `duration_ms` plumbing (possible missing `time` import), and gate1's reliance on private cross-module APIs—fix these and the change is shippable.
